Explain how a VPN works in simple words
12:30 AM

A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet, so nobody in between can see what you send.

Normally, your internet provider and any public Wi-Fi can see which sites you visit. With a VPN, your traffic is locked (encrypted) and sent to the VPN company first. They pass it on to the website for you.

Two things follow from that:

The website sees the VPN's address instead of yours, so your location looks different.
Anyone watching your Wi-Fi sees only scrambled data going to the VPN.

A VPN doesn't make you anonymous. The VPN company can still see your activity, so pick one you trust.
